name: aversion
quote: That painting is ugly as sin.
description: Unattractiveness to the senses or sensibilities in purely subjective arena. What puts something into the zone of 'unattractive' depends on culture and individual experiences. You consider it to be a poorly-formed example of that kind of thing.
perceptions: Something brings dismay by being judged as a poorly-formed instance of its type of thing.
results: preference to not experience this often

comparisons.description: Disgust is the perception that the target could somehow contaminate you. Aversion is simply not liking the thing while not perceiving that it could taint you somehow.
You 'hate' things that you never want to experience again. Aversion is weaker - you find the thing 'poorly-formed' but can probably tolerate experiencing it again.

You can have an aversion to a specific trait or thing without necessarily feeling superior to the person showing it. Contempt involves a more fundamental judgment about the other person's inherent worth or capabilities, leading to a sense of superiority.

variations.name: aesthetic aversion
variations.description: Something unattractive to the senses or sensibilities in purely subjective arena. For example colors you consider clashing or music from a genre you don't favor.
perceptions: An artistic representation of something brings dismay by being considered poorly-formed for that kind of thing.

variations.name: physical aversion
variations.description: A particularly unattractive item, ideal, or person may create a desire to avoid it/him/her. What makes something or someone physically unattractive depends on culture and upbringing.
perceptions: A person or item is judged to be poorly-formed.

variations.name: aversion signaling
variations.description: Sometimes we might recognize that a social group expects us to find a certain thing unappealing, which may nudge us into paying closer attention.
perceptions: We think our social group will want us to dislike this thing.
The thing disappoints by being considered poorly-formed.

guidance.description: If desired, there are various resources available for how to gently resist social pressure.

commentaries.quote: Aesthetic aversion is always subjective. Someone else may appreciate the architecture, singing voice, graffiti, or clashing colors.
A feeling of aversion or attachment toward something is your clue that there's work to be done.
